senses.gloss: m.(b. h.;Shaf. of רוץ) moving creature, esp. unclean reptile.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Ta'anit 1:8">Tosef. Taan. I, 8</cite> <he>אם יהא הש׳ בידו וכ׳</he> if a man has a reptile in his hand, he cannot become clean, even if he bathe &c.; <he>השליך הש׳ וכ׳</he> when he throws the reptile out of his hand, a bath in a basin of forty S’ah avails him (fasting without restitution is of no avail); Y. ib. II, beg. 65ᵃ; Bab. ib. 16ᵃ.
<cite ref="Eruvin 13b:7">Erub. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>היה מטהר את הש׳ וכ׳</he> could prove a reptile to be clean with one hundred and fifty reasons (was a dialectician).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 17a">Snh. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>אין … לטהר ש׳ וכ׳</he> none could be seated in the Sanhedrin, unless he could prove the cleanness of a reptile from Biblical texts; a. fr.—Pl. <he>שְׁרָצִים</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 14:1">Sabb. XIV, 1</cite> <he>שמנה ש׳ וכ׳</he> the eight reptiles mentioned in the Torah (<cite ref="Leviticus 11:29">Lev. XI, 29</cite>, sq.).
<cite ref="Yoma 22b:19">Yoma 22ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="Q01898"><he>פַּרְנָס</he></cite>; a. fr.—<he>פרשת ש׳</he> the section treating of unclean animals, in Sifra Sh’mini.
